The test image shows angular dark brown/black lesions on a soybean leaf with distinct **yellowish-green halos** surrounding darker centers. The lesions appear angular (bounded by veins) and have coalesced in some areas. Some tissue appears to be falling out, creating a ragged appearance.

Key observations:
- Angular lesions bounded by leaf veins
- Dark reddish-brown/black centers
- Prominent yellow-green halos around lesions
- Lesions coalescing into larger irregular areas
- Tissue disruption/falling out in advanced areas

The reference Bacterial Blight images show the same characteristic pattern — angular lesions with yellowish halos — though the test image shows a more advanced/coalesced stage. This matches the Bacterial Blight description perfectly: "dark reddish-brown centers surrounded by yellowish-green halos around water-soaked tissue; lesions may coalesce to form large, irregularly shaped lesions."
